body:
A leaking vape is messy, wasteful and unpleasant to carry, and it can damage devices and clothes. Liquid ends up on your fingers, in your pocket or in the charging port, and a device that leaks keeps leaking until the cause is found. The causes are almost always simple: overfilling, loose or damaged seals, cracks, pressure changes, the wrong liquid thickness, too much airflow, a worn coil or poor storage. This guide explains each one, how to recognize it, how to fix it, how to clean up properly, how to carry devices to avoid leaks and what to do with a device that will not stop leaking. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and liquid should be kept away from children and pets.

## How leaks happen
A vape holds liquid in a reservoir and feeds it to the coil through the wick. The system is designed to keep liquid in the right place using seals, small airflow channels and the balance between liquid, air and pressure. A leak happens when liquid finds a way out: through a gap in a seal, through the airflow, through a crack or out of the fill port. Anything that disturbs the balance, such as too much liquid, a pressure change or a damaged part, can start one.

## Overfilling
Filling a pod or tank to the very top leaves no room for air. Air is needed in the reservoir to let liquid flow smoothly and to cushion changes in pressure. Fill below the max line and never over the central tube, and tilt the tank when you fill it so liquid runs down the side instead of splashing into the airflow channel. Close the fill port firmly. Overfilling is the most common cause of leaks.

## Loose or damaged seals
Check that the pod or tank is tightly seated and that silicone seals are in place and not cracked. A seal that has hardened, stretched or shifted lets liquid past. Replace worn seals if the device uses them, and check them when you change a coil. Make sure the tank is screwed together evenly, not cross-threaded. Do not overtighten, because that can damage the seals.

## Cracked tank or pod
Inspect for hairline cracks, especially after a drop. A crack in plastic or glass is not always visible, and liquid can seep along it. Hold the part up to the light and look for lines or stains. If you find one, replace the part. Do not try to glue it, because the glue will not suit liquid or heat.

## Pressure changes
Flights and driving through mountains can push liquid out. As air pressure falls, the air inside the reservoir expands and pushes liquid out. Keep pods nearly empty when traveling, or choose a sealed disposable. Keep the device upright and in a bag. See [choosing a vape for travel](/blog/best-vapes-for-travel/) and [traveling with vapes](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/).

## Wrong liquid thickness
Thin liquid in a large-coil tank can seep through the coil and leak. Thick liquid can cause flooding if the coil cannot take it. Match liquid to hardware: high-PG liquids can leak from big sub-ohm coils, and high-VG liquids can flood small pods. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). If a particular bottle always leaks in your device, try a different ratio.

## Too much airflow
Very open airflow with a tight coil can cause condensation to pool and run out through the intake. If your device has adjustable airflow, close it a little. Condensation collects in the airflow channel and can drip from the base, which looks like a leak even when the tank is sealed.

## Worn coil
An old coil can flood, because its wicking channels are clogged and liquid builds up around it. Replace it; see [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/). A leak that starts after weeks of normal use often points to the coil.

## Storage position
Store pods and tanks upright. Lying a device on its side lets liquid run toward the airflow and the mouthpiece. In a bag, use a case or a pocket where the device stays upright. Do not leave it in a hot car, because heat thins liquid and expands air.

## Loose connections and threads
If the tank base has a loose thread, liquid can leak through the join. Check the coil is screwed in firmly, and the base is tight. If a thread is damaged, replace the part.

## How to clean up a leak
Wipe the outside with a paper towel while wearing gloves if you can, wash your hands and the surface and dispose of the towels responsibly. Avoid skin contact. Dry the contacts and the charging port before you use or charge the device, because liquid can damage electronics. Keep liquid away from children and pets; see [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/). If liquid has got into the charging port or the electronics, do not charge the device, and let it dry in a warm room, not near heat.

## A step-by-step approach
1. Empty the device and wipe it clean.
2. Inspect the seals, the threads and the body for damage.
3. Check the coil. Replace it if it is worn.
4. Refill below the max line.
5. Seat the pod or tank firmly.
6. Let it rest upright for a few minutes.
7. Test with gentle puffs.
8. If it leaks again, replace the part you suspect, starting with the coil, then the seals, then the pod or tank.

## Disposables that leak
Disposables are sealed, and you cannot open them. A disposable that leaks from the mouthpiece or the base is faulty, or has been damaged or stored badly. Do not use a device that is leaking. Wipe it, keep it upright and contact us with your order ID and photos if it arrived like that. See the [refund policy](/refunds/) and [damaged or missing items](/blog/damaged-or-missing-items-what-to-do/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does my vape leak only when I travel?
Pressure changes push liquid out. Keep pods nearly empty and carry devices upright in a bag.

### Is a little condensation normal?
Yes. A small amount of moisture in the airflow is normal. Wipe it away. A steady drip is a leak.

### Can I use a leaking device?
It is better to fix it first. Liquid on the electronics can damage the device, and you will waste liquid.

### Why does a new pod leak?
It may have been overfilled, not seated properly or have a faulty seal. Remove it, wipe it, refill below the line and seat it firmly.

### Can I stop leaks with tape or glue?
No. Do not modify the device. Replace the faulty part.

## Prevention
Fill carefully, check seals, keep devices upright, avoid heat, match the liquid to the hardware and replace coils on time. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) for replacement parts. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Case studies
### The bag that smelled of fruit
A customer found their bag damp and sweet-smelling after a commute. The pod had been filled to the top and carried on its side. Filling below the line and carrying the device upright stopped it. Lesson: fill level and position decide most leaks.

### The leak after a drop
A tank started leaking two days after it was dropped. A hairline crack had formed in the base, invisible at first. A new tank solved it. Lesson: inspect after a drop, because small cracks cause slow leaks.

### The leak in the cold
A device leaked every winter morning. Cold made the liquid thicker and the seals stiffer. Letting it warm before use, and storing it inside, stopped the leaks. Lesson: temperature changes matter.

## Carrying devices to avoid leaks
Carry devices upright, in a case or a pocket of their own, with the pod nearly empty if you are traveling. Do not put them loose in a bag with keys. Do not leave them in a car. A small silicone sleeve or a case costs little and protects both the device and your belongings.

## A short maintenance routine
Once a week, wipe the outside of the device and check seals and threads. Once a month, rinse refillable tanks and replace worn O-rings. Replace coils and pods on a schedule that suits you. A little routine care stops most leaks before they start.

## Things that look like leaks but are not
Condensation in the mouthpiece, a little moisture around the airflow after a heavy session and liquid that has been spilled during filling can all look like leaks. Wipe the device clean, then watch it for a day. If no new liquid appears, it was not a leak.

## Frequently asked questions about leaks
### Can I fix a cracked tank with glue?
No. Glue is not suited to liquid or heat, and it can contaminate the liquid. Replace the part.

### Why does my vape leak when it is full but not when it is half full?
A full tank leaves little air, and any pressure change pushes liquid out. Fill to about three-quarters when traveling.

### Does a leaking vape need a new coil?
Often yes. Try a fresh coil first, because a worn coil is a common cause. If it still leaks, check the seals and the tank.

### Will leaks damage my device?
Liquid on the contacts or the port can cause corrosion and misfires. Wipe and dry the device, and do not charge it until the port is dry.
